THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by accused No.1 in crime No.108/2023 registered at K.M.Doddi police station, praying to set aside the order dated 01.08.2023 passed by the Court of V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Mandya, whereby his application filed under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been rejected.

entities.text: Court of V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Mandya
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. I have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned HCGP for the State and the learned counsel for respondent No.2/complainant.

3. Crime No.108/2023 of K.M.Doddi police station is registered against the appellant/accused No.1,
his parents and sister for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 323, 506, 316, 341 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections NC: 2023:KHC:41301 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s), 3(2)(va), 3(1)w of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 (hereinafter referred to as 'Act' for short), on a complaint lodged by respondent No.2, wife of appellant/accused No.1.
4.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is alleged that the first informant's marriage was performed with accused No.1 on 19.12.2021 and it was a love and inter-caste marriage.
For the said reason, the first informant was residing separately with accused No.1 at Bengaluru.

In their wedlock, she gave birth to a child and thereafter,
she started residing with the family members of her husband.
It is alleged that during her stay in the house of her in-laws, she was abused with reference to her caste, threatened, assaulted and subjected to torture etc.
It is further alleged that when she became pregnant for the second time, the accused forcibly made her to drink some herbal water, due to which, she suffered abortion.

sentences.text: The further allegations are that the accused persons have demanded a sum of Rs.5,00,000/-, abused her by insulting her caste, quarreled etc.
5. While filing the charge sheet the offence under Section 316 of IPC has been deleted as there was no material NC: 2023:KHC:41301 to show that the accused persons have committed the said offence.
6. Accused Nos.2 to 4 namely, parents and sister of accused No.1 have been enlarged on bail.
The complaint averments go to show that the marriage between the complainant and the appellant was a love marriage and both of them were living separately in Bengaluru initially.
7. The complainant/respondent No.2, who is present before the Court submits that she has a small child and she wants to live with her husband.

8. The learned Sessions Judge while rejecting the prayer for bail has observed that caste discrimination is prima- facie found and there is specific bar contained under Section 18 of the Act,
since there exists prima-facie case and sufficient reasons to believe the involvement of the accused in the commission of offence.
However, under Section 18 of the Act, bar is to grant anticipatory bail if there is a prima-facie case and not regular bail.
9. A perusal of the material on record reveals that on account of a matrimonial dispute, the complaint came to be NC: 2023:KHC:41301 lodged against the accused persons.
However, no opinion can be expressed on the merits of the case.

Considering the fact that while filing the charge sheet, the offence under Section 316 of IPC has been deleted and accused Nos.2 to 4 are already enlarged on bail, the relief sought by the appellant can be granted, keeping in view the statement made by the victim.
The investigation is completed and charge sheet is also filed.
Hence, in the facts and circumstances, by imposing necessary conditions, the appellant can be admitted to bail.

Hence, the following:
ORDER
The appeal is allowed.
The order dated 01.08.2023 passed by the Court of V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Mandya is set aside.
